source.title: Periodic Readout Induces a First-Order Generalization Transition in a Quantum Perceptron
source.authors: Fabio Benatti; Masoud Gharahi; Giovanni Gramegna; Stefano Mancini; Vincenzo Parisi

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies a teacher–student quantum perceptron with periodic readout. It does not train standard deep networks on random labels or test any of the six claim versions; random-label storage is mentioned as prior work.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work for increased random-pattern storage capacity but does not report its own random-label experiment. Its own result on perfect training classification with chance-level generalization uses teacher-generated labels and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes equilibrium inference in a periodic-readout quantum perceptron with teacher-generated labels. It reports no independent random-label intervention, deep-network SGD experiment, corruption sweep, or comparison of real-label and noise learning over training. Increased random-label storage capacity is attributed to prior work [8].
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors attribute increased random-pattern storage capacity to prior work and find that periodic readout suppresses initial teacher alignment and, above a critical frequency, produces a first-order equilibrium generalization transition as training load increases. At fixed finite load, their replica-symmetric prediction approaches chance generalization as frequency grows, despite perfect training classification. They also identify metastability and initialization-dependent GAMP behavior, while the large-load asymptotic generalization error remains frequency independent.
record.recipe_differences: Teacher–student Bayesian analysis of a square-wave quantum perceptron using replica-symmetric theory; no deep-network stochastic-gradient training or random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Readout frequency λ changes the learning curve and equilibrium generalization; for λ > λc the transition is first-order.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed finite training load, the replica-symmetric equilibrium prediction gives teacher–student overlap tending to zero and Gibbs generalization error tending to 1/2 as readout frequency increases without bound. Posterior samples classify all training examples correctly by construction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A periodic-readout perceptron can have perfect classification of teacher-generated training labels while its equilibrium generalization approaches chance at high readout frequency.

record.problems: The main learning curves are replica-symmetric predictions. The authors note that a proof for binary inputs and a discontinuous channel remains open; the finite-size GAMP comparison uses N = 4000 and two independent instances per point.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks using stochastic gradient methods, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Deep-network fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels, and differences between real-label and random-label training trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: Training load is sample count per input dimension, not training time; varying readout frequency is not varying label corruption. Random Rademacher inputs and Gaussian limiting local fields do not establish V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error under random labels, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption rises.
Fitting shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: quantum perceptron with periodic readout sλ
rows.size_stated: N-dimensional input; thermodynamic limit N, P → ∞ at fixed α = P/N
rows.operation_detail: Replica-symmetric equilibrium prediction of Gibbs-student training and generalization error for teacher-generated labels
rows.measure: training classification and Gibbs generalization error
rows.value: perfect classification of all training examples; εg → 1/2
rows.note: The labels are generated by a teacher using the same periodic classifier, not randomized. The result is an RS prediction, not a deep-network SGD experiment.
rows.check: The stated outcome is supported, but cannot establish any claim version. Labels follow a teacher rule, and perfect training classification holds by construction for posterior samples restricted to compatible weights; it is not evidence that an optimizer fits arbitrary labels. The operation should be theoretical equilibrium analysis rather than measurement. Proposition 2 establishes the chance-error limit within the replica-symmetric prediction.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
